level1.2: WriteLn outputs text to the screen.
level1.3: Use WriteLn('Hello World!'); to output the text.

level2.1: Variables must be declared in the 'var' section.
level2.3: Example: var number: Integer; and then number := 42;

level3.1: You can output multiple values in one WriteLn.
level3.2: Separate values with commas: WriteLn(a, ' + ', b, ' = ', sum);
level3.3: First calculate sum := a + b; and then output the result.

level4.1: String is the data type for text.
level4.3: Assign: name := 'Pascal'; and output: WriteLn('Hello, ', name, '!');

level5.1: Write outputs text without a line break.
level5.2: ReadLn waits for input and stores it.

level6.2: The structure is: if condition then statement else statement;
level6.3: if number >= 0 then WriteLn('Positive') else WriteLn('Negative');

level7.1: for loops count from a start to an end value.
level7.2: for i := 1 to 5 do executes code 5 times.
level7.3: for i := 1 to 5 do WriteLn(i); outputs 1 to 5.

level8.1: while repeats as long as a condition is true.
level8.2: You must use begin-end for multiple statements.
level8.3: while count > 0 do begin WriteLn(count); count := count - 1; end;

level9.1: Procedures are defined before the main program.
level9.2: procedure Name(Parameter: Type); starts a procedure.
level9.3: procedure Greet(name: String); begin WriteLn('Hello, ', name); end;

level10.2: The return type is specified after the function name.
level10.3: function Square(n: Integer): Integer; begin Square := n * n; end;
